Commentary.Commentary: ...THE CHASE...

Bangladesh used 7 bowlers but the spinners again took the credit. They didn't start well, there was not much in the pitch for seamers and went for plenty. However, Mahedi Hasan and Mehidy Hasan got some calmness and stem to run flow by bowling tight. Not their best performance but looking at the pitch, Bangladesh will hope to chase it down.
Kusal Perera has not recovered from the injury suffered and won't be able to participate any more with the bat. As it stands, Kusal Perera is retired out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: Kusal Perera has not recovered from the injury suffered and won't be able to participate any more with the bat. As it stands, Kusal Perera is retired out.

Commentary.Commentary: A decent score by Sri Lanka. They will be happy with how the last couple of overs went as that gave them an extra cushion. Sri Lanka got off to a blistering start. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera were superb on top. Kusal Mendis kept the run rate in check but once he got out, Sri Lanka got a bit fragile. Their middle-order didn't click much but Dhananjaya de Silva got things back on track with fine fifty. There were a couple of cameos at the back end as well.
OUT! This is full and outside off, well wide. Hemantha looks to drag it across but gets a top edge to covers where Mustafizur Rahman takes it. Was the back of the hand delivery.

Hello and welcome to the first Warm Up game between two Asian sides, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. The Bangla Tigers have a good opportunity to get their best playing XI. They didn't had the best of Asia Cuo recently but their bowling side showed promising signs in the tournament. They will hope their batting clicks in this warm-up games. Sri Lanka on the other hand will be confident coming into the World Cup. With similar conditions and runners-up in the Asia cup. They look pretty good for the upcoming tournament. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.
... Match Day...

The ICC ODI World Cup 2023 is closer than ever, but before the main event, the teams will have the opportunity to prepare themselves and get their combinations right in the warm-up matches. The first game is between two Asian rivals, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka at the Barsapara Stadium in Guwahati. The former side will be led by the number-one-ranked ICC all-rounder, Shakib Al Hasan. Their squad selection wasn't without controversy as they left Tamim Iqbal out of the squad due to internal conflicts among the players. They will have to keep all that behind them and focus on the job in their hands. The Bangla Tigers don't have a good record against the Lankans as they also lost to them in the recently concluded Asia Cup. The batting department will depend on the likes of Litton Das, Najmul Hossain Shanto, and in-form Towhid Hridoy while the skipper along with Mushfiqur Rahim and Mehidy Hasan, will give them much-needed experience in the middle order. They will surely miss the services of Ebadot Hossain, but Mustafizur Rahman, Hasan Mahmud, and Shoriful Islam make up a decent pace attack. On the spin front, Shakib leads from the front with Nasum Ahmed and Mehidy. They will want to get a win here to boost their confidence going into the group stages. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, were battered by India in the Asia Cup final and they probably needed a break to recover from that. Another setback for them is that Wanindu Hasaranga won't be part of this World Cup due to an injury. Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis, Dhananjaya de Silva, and Charith Asalanka form the core of this batting line-up and the side would like them to do well in this warm-up game. Dimuth Karunaratne, Sadeera Samarawickrama, and Dasun Shanaka haven’t been in the best of form in recent months, and the side would like to see them get decent match practice before the tournament starts. Shanaka will hope to use the resources available to him effectively and efficiently. In the absence of Hasaranga, the onus will be on Maheesh Theekshana to lead the spin attack along with young Dunith Wellalage who showed his skills and great potential in the Asia Cup. Kasun Rajitha, Dilshan Madushanka, and Matheesha Pathirana will have the responsibility to handle the pace department which on paper looks a bit bleak, but before losing to India, they were on a brilliant unbeaten run in this format and will hope to repeat something like that again. It will be interesting to see how the two teams shape up for this game and which players put their best foot forward. Let's see who comes out on top.
